text:
B: Alright? Can you hear me yeah?
A: Yeah, I can hear you! Hiya, I'm Lauren. Sorry, me cat's just walked across the table, ignore her. Well, him. Biscuit.
B: Biscuit, that's a proper good name. I'm Callum. How's it going?
A: Yeah, good, ta. Bit knackered. How was that puzzle thing for you? I was rubbish, I just kept clicking stuff.
B: Same, mate, honestly. I think I just guessed half of it. Where are you, then?
A: Derby. Chaddesden. Do you know Derby?
B: Only 'cos of football really. I'm Plymouth, so like, Argyle.
A: Oh, me dad'd love you. Me and him go to the Rams sometimes, and I'm the one who shouts at the telly. He just sits there going "calm down, Lauren".
B: Ha, nah, I'm the same at Home Park. If I can get a cheap ticket. Or blag someone's spare.
A: So what d'you do? You at uni or something? You look young, sorry, that sounds awful.
B: Nah, you're alright. Yeah, second year, business and management. And I work at a pub on the Barbican, glass collecting, pot washing, that sort of thing. Weekends mostly.
A: Oh, nice. Do you get good tips?
B: Sometimes, yeah. Had a stag do in last weekend, they were proper generous, like. Bunged me a twenty for basically just being there.
A: Twenty quid! That's amazing. I used to be a fitness instructor, at the leisure centre, but erm, they changed who runs it and they cut loads of classes, so my job sort of went. So I'm, you know, looking. I do the odd cover class. Signing on, the glamorous life.
B: Ah, that's rubbish, sorry. What kind of classes was it?
A: Zumba, step, circuits. I love it, I love being at the front, getting all the nervous ones going, do you know what I mean? Like the older ladies who come in all scared and then six weeks later they're giving it everything.
B: That's quite cool, actually. I've got a gym membership. I use it, like, in bursts.
A: Everyone does! Three weeks keen and then gone. I can always tell.
B: Yeah, nah, that's me exactly, caught out. What else d'you get up to, then?
A: Erm, charity shops, I'm obsessed. I got a nineties windbreaker last week for three quid, proper retro, all purple and teal.
B: Three quid? Mate, you need to be flipping that. I do Vinted, trainers mostly. Got some Jordans the other week, made forty quid on them.
A: Shut up, forty quid?
B: Yeah, I've got a bit of a system going. Buy cheap, clean them up, sell. A nineties windbreaker, people'd go mad for that.
A: I'm not selling it though, I look amazing in it! Sorry, I'm going off on one. But that's actually a good shout, like, the ones I don't wear.
B: You should, honestly. Easy money. You could do, like, a whole retro page.
A: Maybe. Me boyfriend Ryan'd be chuffed, he says the spare room's just bags of clothes now. So what do you wanna do after uni?
B: Erm, kind of sales, maybe. Or start something. Haven't really worked it out yet, I'll be—
